translationRepairs: Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, military commissioner of Dai and younger brother of the Martial Emperor's mother.
Li Sizhao, whose courtesy name was Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, prefect of Dai and younger full brother of the Martial Emperor.
母弟 means a younger brother by the same mother, not the mother's brother; 刺史 is prefect, not military commissioner.
Li Sizhao, courtesy name Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, military commissioner of Dai and younger brother of the Martial Emperor's mother.
Li Sizhao, courtesy name Yiguang, was the adopted son of Kerou, prefect of Dai Prefecture and younger full brother of the Martial Emperor.
母弟 is the Martial Emperor's younger full brother; 刺史 is prefect of Dai, not military commissioner.
(The Ouyang History records that he was originally surnamed Han and came from a common family in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)〉
(The Ouyang History records that he was originally surnamed Han and came from a common family in Dagu County, Fen Prefecture.)
A stray Chinese closing-annotation mark 〉 was left at the end of the English sentence.

In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and was promoted to acting Grand Mentor for his service.

In the fourth year he was made commander of the inner guard, returned to aid Hezhong, routed Bian forces at Hubi Fort, captured the Bian general Hua Li, and for his service was promoted to acting Vice Director.
檢校僕射 is an acting vice-director rank, not Grand Mentor. The revision translates the office rather than leaving Pushe unexplained.
In Guanghua 3 the Bian attacked Cangzhou. Liu Rengong appealed for help, and Sizhao was sent through Xing and Mo to relieve him.
In Guanghua 3 the Bian attacked Cangzhou. Liu Rengong appealed for help, and Sizhao was sent through Xing and Ming to relieve him.
He then attacked and captured Mo Prefecture, taking its commander Zhu Shaozong prisoner.
He then attacked and captured Ming Prefecture, taking its commander Zhu Shaozong prisoner.
洺州 is Ming Prefecture, not Mo Prefecture.
In the ninth month the Liang founder led thirty thousand men in person to Linmo, while Ge Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
In the ninth month the Liang founder led thirty thousand men in person to Linming, while Ge Congzhou laid an ambush at Qingshan Pass.
臨洺 is Linming, not Linmo.

The Martial Emperor was about to follow this advice; Sizhao urgently argued that it must not be done. Still undecided, he was saved when Grand Consort Liu spoke forcefully within, and the Martial Emperor then stopped.
The Martial Emperor was about to follow this advice; Sizhao urgently argued against it. Still undecided, he desisted only after Grand Consort Liu spoke forcefully against it from within.
賴 introduces Grand Consort Liu as the reason the proposal was abandoned; 武皇 is the subject who finally desisted. This preserves that logic in natural English.
Sizhao governed Ze and Lu, holding offices from Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian up to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
Sizhao governed Ze and Lu, holding offices from Minister of Education (Situ) and Grand Guardian up to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
司徒 is Minister of Education / Grand Preceptor of the Masses, not Grand Preceptor (太師), which appears only in the next sentence as a posthumous gift.

When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made military commissioner of Dai.

When the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, he served under Zhou Dewei at Yuyu. Siben led cavalry in daily skirmishes with the Bian, presented more than a thousand captives in all, and was made prefect of Dai.
代州刺史 is prefect of Dai, not military commissioner.

In the twelfth year Zhuangzong secured Weibo while Liu Yan held Shen County. Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he helped defeat Liu Yan at Old Yuancheng and recovered Mo, Ci, and Wei.

In the twelfth year Zhuangzong secured Weibo while Liu Xun held Shen County. Siben was ordered into Taiyuan to guard the capital. In the thirteenth year he helped defeat Liu Xun at Old Yuancheng and recovered Ming, Ci, and Wei.
洺 is Ming Prefecture, not Mo, and 劉鄩 is Liu Xun rather than Liu Yan. The revision corrects both names while retaining Shen County for 莘縣.
(The Ouyang History records that Si'en was originally from the Tuyuhun people.)〉
(The Ouyang History records that Si'en was originally from the Tuyuhun people.)
A stray Chinese closing-annotation mark 〉 remains at the end of the English.
At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of military commissioner of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.
At the battle of Shen he was rewarded with the post of prefect of Dai and overall commander of troops north of Shiling Pass, and was later promoted to military commissioner of Zhenwu.
代州刺史 is prefect of Dai; only 振武節度使 is a military commissionership.
Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Ming, mindful of old service, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Commandant.
Early in the Tiancheng era Emperor Mingzong, mindful of old service, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.
明宗 is Emperor Mingzong; 詔贈太尉 is a posthumous honorary appointment, not an enfeoffment.
